package_info.package_manager: N/A (custom malware, not distributed via public package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (botnet malware, not versioned as a package)
package_info.why_malicious: FritzFrog is a custom-built, fileless, peer-to-peer (P2P) botnet written in Go that targets SSH servers. It operates entirely in memory, propagates by brute-forcing SSH credentials, and is used for Monero cryptomining. Its decentralized architecture, in-memory execution, and ability to spread laterally make it highly evasive and suitable for persistent, large-scale infrastructure abuse.

execution_context.trigger: After successful SSH brute-force login and process injection
execution_context.file_location: memory (fileless, runs as an in-memory process on the compromised SSH server)
required_permissions: network (for SSH brute-force and P2P communication)
process execution (to launch cryptominer and maintain persistence)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Custom Go code that, after brute-forcing SSH credentials, injects itself into memory, establishes encrypted P2P connections with other infected nodes, downloads a Monero cryptominer binary (such as xmrig) to a temporary location, and executes it as a child process. The code also listens for and relays P2P commands, enabling lateral movement and further propagation.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After successful SSH brute-force and in-memory process injection, the code establishes encrypted P2P connections with other infected hosts, downloads a Monero cryptominer binary to a temporary directory, executes the cryptominer as a child process, and relays P2P commands to propagate to additional SSH servers, resulting in unauthorized resource usage, lateral movement, and botnet expansion.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code operates entirely in memory without leaving files on disk, spreads autonomously via SSH brute-forcing, establishes decentralized encrypted P2P connections, and launches unauthorized cryptomining processes, all of which are hallmarks of advanced botnet malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate SSH server processes do not inject code into memory, form decentralized P2P networks, brute-force other SSH servers, or launch cryptomining operations without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate distributed computing frameworks may use P2P communication and in-memory processing, but do not propagate via credential brute-forcing or execute unauthorized cryptomining payloads.
key_indicators: Fileless, in-memory process injection on SSH servers
Autonomous SSH brute-force attacks originating from the compromised host
Encrypted P2P network formation without central command and control
On-the-fly download and execution of cryptominer binaries (e.g., xmrig) in temporary directories
Relay of P2P commands for lateral movement and further propagation

attack_chain.action: Brute-forces SSH credentials to gain unauthorized access to the target server.
attack_chain.leads_to: In-memory process injection and enrollment into the P2P botnet

attack_chain.action: Injects itself into memory and establishes encrypted P2P connections with other infected nodes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of Monero cryptominer and lateral movement

attack_chain.action: Downloads a Monero cryptominer binary (such as xmrig) to a temporary directory and executes it as a child process, using the server's resources for illicit mining.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ongoing resource abuse, botnet expansion, and further SSH brute-force attacks

behavioral_signatures: Fileless, in-memory process injection on SSH servers with no corresponding executable on disk
Unusual outbound SSH connections to random or previously uncontacted IP addresses (indicative of P2P botnet formation)
Unauthorized cryptominer process execution (e.g., xmrig) running as a child of an unknown or suspicious process
High frequency of SSH brute-force login attempts originating from internal or newly compromised hosts
Processes listening on non-standard ports associated with encrypted P2P traffic
file_indicators: Absence of malware files on disk despite suspicious process activity
Unexpected cryptominer binaries (e.g., xmrig) present in /tmp, /var/tmp, or other temporary directories
Processes with no corresponding binary on disk (indicative of in-memory execution)
network_indicators: High volume of SSH traffic to and from non-standard or random IP addresses
Encrypted P2P traffic between infected nodes, often on high, non-standard ports, with no central C2 server
Outbound connections to known Monero mining pool domains or IP addresses
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor SSH servers for in-memory only processes, especially those establishing multiple outbound SSH connections or exhibiting P2P-like encrypted traffic patterns on non-standard ports. Detect brute-force login attempts and unauthorized cryptominer processes, particularly those running from temporary directories or as children of unknown processes. Use network monitoring to identify encrypted P2P traffic and connections to known Monero mining pools. Correlate anomalous resource usage (CPU, network) with these indicators to confirm infection.
